quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #2
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 18

questions.question: When a flagger is directing traffic in a construction zone, you must:

options.text: Follow the flagger's directions.
Do what other drivers are doing, even if it goes against the flagger's instructions.
Assume the flagger should not be directing traffic.
Follow the normal traffic laws as if the area was not under construction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow the flagger's directions.
questions.explanation: Be ready to slow down and be careful when a sign, flagger, or police officer tells you to do so. Not following their instructions is illegal and dangerous to construction workers.

questions.question: If another driver cuts you off in traffic, you should:

options.text: Pull next to the driver and yell at them.
Stay calm and move on.
Flash your high beams at the driver.
Cut off the other driver to get even.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay calm and move on.
questions.explanation: To avoid road rage, do not take it personally if another driver cuts you off. Just stay calm and continue driving safely.

questions.question: You have a green light at an intersection, but pedestrians are crossing against the red light. You should:

options.text: Honk your horn.
Speed up and drive in front of the pedestrians.
Stop and let the pedestrians cross safely.
Drive close to the pedestrians to scare them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and let the pedestrians cross safely.
questions.explanation: Yield to pedestrians and other vehicles that are in the intersection when you have a green light. Always be careful around pedestrians.

questions.question: If you miss your exit on an interstate expressway:

options.text: Stop and make a U-turn.
Exit at the next exit and come back to the exit you missed.
Roll down your window and ask the driver next to you for help.
Back up on the highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Exit at the next exit and come back to the exit you missed.
questions.explanation: Do not back up or turn around on the highway if you miss your exit. Go to the next exit and safely turn around.

questions.question: You should always signal when:

options.text: Changing lanes.
Pulling into or out of a parking space.
Pulling into traffic from an alley or parking area.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Always use your turn signal when changing lanes, pulling into or out of a parking space, or pulling into traffic from an alley or parking area. This tells other drivers what you are doing and helps prevent accidents.

questions.question: When you hear a fire engine siren behind you, you must:

options.text: Slow down until it passes you.
Turn on your flashers.
Pull over to the side of the road and stop.
Speed up and take the nearest exit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over to the side of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: When you hear an emergency vehicle siren, you must pull over to the curb or side of the road and stop.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Slow down and be ready to stop if cars are coming.
Come to a complete stop, then go when it is safe.
Drive carefully through the intersection without always stopping.
Stop only if there is traffic on the intersecting road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop, then go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: A stop sign means you must come to a complete stop. Let vehicles and pedestrians in the intersection go first. Then go when it is safe.

questions.question: You notice the driver ahead is driving with one hand and talking to a passenger. You should:

options.text: Give that vehicle extra space.
Know that this driver is less safe because they are not paying attention.
Do not drive the same way.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Do not get distracted by passengers, looking for things in your car, reading, or daydreaming while driving. If a driver near you seems distracted, give them extra space because they are more likely to have an accident.

questions.question: Alcohol:

options.text: Slows your reflexes and reaction time.
Puts you to sleep.
Wakes you up.
Improves your judgment.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slows your reflexes and reaction time.
questions.explanation: Alcohol is a drug that slows your brain and reduces the skills you need to drive safely. It slows your reaction time and impairs your judgment.

questions.question: What is the only way to lower your blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?

options.text: Drink coffee.
Exercise.
Give your body time to process the alcohol.
Take a cold shower.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give your body time to process the alcohol.
questions.explanation: The only way to lower your BAC is to wait for your body to break down the alcohol over time. Coffee, exercise, and cold showers can help you stay awake, but they cannot lower your BAC or make you sober.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: No passing zone.
Winding road.
Pedestrian crossing.
Low ground railroad crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low ground railroad crossing.
questions.explanation: This sign warns of a low ground railroad crossing. At this location, railroad tracks cross the road at a steep angle. The bottom of low vehicles may drag or get stuck on the tracks.

questions.question: Tailgating is:

options.text: Illegal.
Inconvenient, but nothing more.
The fastest way to get to where you're going.
The best way to let drivers know they aren't driving fast enough.

questions.correctAnswerText: Illegal.
questions.explanation: Tailgating is illegal. It is a main cause of rear-end crashes. The fine for tailgating can be as high as $100.

questions.question: If you leave your vehicle unattended, you must:

options.text: Turn off the engine.
Lock the ignition and remove the key.
Set the parking brake.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: When you leave your vehicle unattended, you must turn off the engine, lock the ignition, remove the key, and set the parking brake.

questions.question: What is a good way to avoid fatigue on a long trip?

options.text: Stop and rest every two hours.
Do arm exercises every hour.
Drive with one eye open at a time.
Change feet on the gas pedal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and rest every two hours.
questions.explanation: On a long trip, stop every two hours for a short break to avoid fatigue. If you feel drowsy, pull off the road safely and take a nap, or find a place to stay for the night.

questions.question: Before changing lanes on a multilane highway, you should:

options.text: Sound your horn.
Turn on your headlights.
Reduce your speed.
Check your mirrors and blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors and blind spots.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, look in your rearview and side mirrors to make sure no one is passing you. Also look over your shoulder to check your blind spot.

questions.question: What are the most effective safety restraints in a traffic crash?

options.text: Only a lap and shoulder belt.
Only an airbag.
Both a lap/shoulder belt and an airbag.
No safety restraints.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both a lap/shoulder belt and an airbag.
questions.explanation: Safety belts double your chance of surviving a crash and more than double your chance of avoiding serious injury. Airbags used with safety belts provide extra protection in a front-end crash. Wear both shoulder and lap belts.

questions.question: Why shouldn't you follow other cars too closely?

options.text: You may not see the road between the cars.
You may not have time to stop if the vehicle in front slows or stops suddenly.
You may not see the vehicle's turn signals.
You may not see the other vehicle's brake lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may not have time to stop if the vehicle in front slows or stops suddenly.
questions.explanation: If you follow too closely and the vehicle in front slows or stops suddenly, you may not have enough time to avoid a collision.

questions.question: Why can night driving be more difficult than day driving?

options.text: Cars overheat more quickly at night.
You can't see as well in the dark.
It is more likely to be raining at night.
You are more likely to encounter a motorcycle at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can't see as well in the dark.
questions.explanation: At night, your vision is reduced. Always use appropriate headlights. Drive slowly enough that you can stop within the distance you can see ahead.

questions.question: How should you safely cross a railroad?

options.text: Look both ways, but only when the red light is flashing.
Listen, look both ways, and then cross if it is safe.
Cross as quickly as possible when a train is approaching.
Quickly pass under any lowering gates.

questions.correctAnswerText: Listen, look both ways, and then cross if it is safe.
questions.explanation: Railroad crossings are always dangerous. Look and listen for trains coming from either direction before crossing the tracks. Wait for signals showing a train is approaching and never cross until you are sure it is safe.

questions.question: When you see a steady yellow traffic light, you should:

options.text: Speed up to avoid a red light.
Keep driving because you have the right-of-way.
Slow down and stop, unless you are already in the intersection.
Check what the cars next to you are doing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and stop, unless you are already in the intersection.
questions.explanation: A steady yellow light means a red light is coming next. Stop unless you are already in the intersection.

questions.question: A pedestrian starts to cross in front of your vehicle. What should you do?

options.text: Flash your lights.
Slow down.
Speed up and pass in front of the pedestrian.
Stop and let the pedestrian cross.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and let the pedestrian cross.
questions.explanation: When you see pedestrians on or crossing the road, slow down and be ready to stop. Be extra careful where children are present. You must always let pedestrians cross in a crosswalk.

questions.question: You missed your exit on the freeway. What should you do?

options.text: Go to the next exit.
Make a U-turn through the median.
Pull onto the shoulder and back your car to the exit.
Flag down a police officer for an escort back to your exit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Go to the next exit.
questions.explanation: If you miss your exit, take the next exit. Do not stop, back up, swerve across lanes, or cross the median. These actions are illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: Who must wear a safety belt in a motor vehicle?

options.text: Only the driver
Only adult passengers
Only passengers under the age of 16
All the vehicle's occupants

questions.correctAnswerText: All the vehicle's occupants
questions.explanation: The law requires everyone in a motor vehicle to wear a safety belt or use a child passenger restraint. Drivers and passengers 16 and older can be fined $25 for not wearing a safety belt.

questions.question: An emergency vehicle is approaching with flashing red or blue lights. What should you do?

options.text: See if you can reach your destination before the emergency vehicle catches up to you.
Continue driving but try to stay out of its way.
Pull over to the side of the road and come to a complete stop.
Stop in the middle of an intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over to the side of the road and come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: You must yield to all emergency vehicles with sirens or flashing lights. Pull over to the right edge of the road when possible. If you are in an intersection, drive through it first before pulling over.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Cars in right lane must slow down.
No left turn.
Merge.
Pass only in the right lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Merge.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that two lanes of traffic moving in the same direction will become one lane.
